evidence_chain.link: The quote from the knowledge chunk supports the idea that right heart obstructive lesions (B3) can cause severe cyanosis in early infancy.

evidence_chain.link: The quote from the knowledge chunk contrasts with the idea that left heart obstructive lesions (B1) typically cause heart failure signs at a later age.
evidence_chain.quote: Complete AV septal defect with a large left-to-right shunt causes signs of heart failure (HF—eg, tachypnea, dyspnea with feeding, poor weight gain, diaphoresis) by age 4 to 6 wk.

ranked_facts.why: The fact that the infant is experiencing cyanosis, tachypnea, and poor feeding in early infancy is more consistent with right heart obstructive lesions (B3) than with left heart obstructive lesions (B1).
